A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QPA study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across appendix relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantum-circuit simulation and language-model fine-tuning results on WikiText-2 and Penn Treebank, including perplexity comparisons and parameter-efficiency analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds original circuit, finite-shot, simulated-noise, gradient-variance, and computational-time results.

M1.justification: The central QPA generator, mapping network, chunking procedure, and training equations remain unchanged. Appendix F introduces explicit RX+CNOT, RXRZ+CNOT, and RYRZ+CNOT generator variants alongside the original RY+CNOT circuit, constituting a limited architectural extension.

E1.justification: WikiText-2 and Penn Treebank language-modeling coverage is retained. Appendix G adds finite-shot execution and noise models from ibm_torino and ibm_fez as simulated quantum-execution test environments; no new language dataset or downstream task is introduced.

E2.justification: The original LoRA, DoRA, PT, and FFA benchmark comparisons remain. Figure 7 extends the LoRA/QPA comparison with three additional evaluated circuit comparators: RX+CNOT, RXRZ+CNOT, and RYRZ+CNOT.

E3.justification: V2 adds substantial evaluation protocols: measurement budgets of 10, 20, and 40 times 2^N; hardware-derived noise simulations; and approximately matched-time comparisons using fewer QPA epochs. Tables 4–7 retain existing training settings. The reported qubit range changes from 13–20 to 4–11, without establishing reruns; Figure 4(a) still displays the old range.

E4.justification: New Appendices F–I investigate circuit choice, finite-shot sensitivity, hardware-derived noise, gradient behavior associated with barren plateaus, and performance under comparable execution time. These substantially extend the existing rank, chunk-size, and circuit-depth analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts, random seeds, performance confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. V2's gradient-variance plots are trainability diagnostics, rather than uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance; measurement-shot budgets specify simulation sampling.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their benchmark values, including GPT-2 QPA-LoRA perplexity 1.583 versus LoRA's 1.595. Figures 7–11 and Tables 8–9 add circuit, sampling, noise, gradient, epoch-budget, and timing results. Newly reported GPT-2 batch times are 0.0460 seconds for QPA versus 0.0154 seconds for LoRA. The textual qubit range also changes, although Figure 4(a) remains inconsistent with it.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds mathematical definitions of alternative circuit constructions in Equations 12–14. Existing gradient and chunking equations remain unchanged, while the cited error bound and measurement-shot complexity bound survive relocation and renumbering. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, principal contributions, and headline parameter-reduction and perplexity claims remain substantively unchanged. The conclusion revises the claimed near-term quantum-resource requirement from 13–20 to 4–11 qubits, changing a specific practical-feasibility claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of noise as a potentially helpful perturbation, the mapping network's possible influence on gradient behavior, and the reduced advantage under comparable computational time. These extend v1's largely prospective discussion of practical quantum execution. Actual hardware validation remains future work.

D1.justification: V1's implementation appendix containing PyTorch/TorchQuantum code for layer replacement and parameter generation is removed, without an equivalent listing elsewhere in v2. V2 adds execution-time information and noise-backend and shot-budget specifications. Existing mapping-network, training-hyperparameter, and GPU disclosures remain; the code deletion does not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting noise and gradient discussions, including Domingo et al., Wu et al., McClean et al., Zhang et al., and Glorot and Bengio. This is a focused expansion; the central positioning relative to PEFT and quantum parameter generation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section structure are retained. Changes include localized introduction editing, paragraph regrouping, author-order and affiliation corrections, and a conference header. Appendices are reorganized, including relocation of the finite-shot discussion from B to G.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual presentation through Figures 7–11 and runtime Tables 8–9, covering the new diagnostic and computational analyses. It removes the implementation listings, relocates retained appendix displays, and reformats existing main figures. Figures 5–6 retain identical graphical content.

improvement.justification: The added finite-shot/noise simulations and approximately matched-time comparisons make practical feasibility substantially easier to assess, including revealing QPA's roughly threefold simulation overhead. The net improvement is limited by removal of the implementation code and the unresolved discrepancy between v2's 4–11-qubit text and Figure 4(a)'s retained 13–20-qubit display.
